verses.1:1: That which was from the beginning, which we have heard, which we have seen with our eyes, which we beheld, and our hands touched, concerning the Word of life—
verses.1:2: and the life was manifested, and we have seen, and we bear witness and proclaim to you the eternal life which was with the Father and was manifested to us—
verses.1:3: what we have seen and heard we proclaim to you as well, so that you likewise may share fellowship with us; and our fellowship is indeed with the Father and with His Son Jesus Christ.
verses.1:4: And these things we write, that our joy may be made full.
verses.1:5: And this is the message which we have heard from Him and announce to you: that God is light, and in Him there is no darkness at all.
verses.1:6: If we say that we have fellowship with Him, yet walk in the darkness, we are lying and do not do the truth;
verses.1:7: but if we walk in the light, as He Himself is in the light, we have fellowship one with another, and the blood of Jesus His Son cleanses us from every sin.
verses.1:8: If we say that we have no sin, we lead ourselves astray, and the truth is not in us.
verses.1:9: If we confess our sins, He is faithful and righteous, that He may forgive us our sins and cleanse us from all unrighteousness.
verses.1:10: If we say that we have not sinned, we make Him out to be a liar, and His word is not in us.
verses.2:1: My little children, these things I write to you, that you may not sin. And if anyone should sin, we have an Advocate with the Father, Jesus Christ the righteous.
verses.2:2: And He Himself is the propitiation for our sins, yet not for ours alone, but also for the whole world.
verses.2:3: And in this we know that we have known Him, if we keep His commandments.
verses.2:4: The one who says, "I have known Him," yet does not keep His commandments, is a liar, and the truth is not in him.
verses.2:5: But whoever keeps His word, truly in him the love of God has been brought to perfection. By this we know that we are in Him:
verses.2:6: he who says he abides in Him ought himself to walk even as He walked.
verses.2:7: Beloved, it is no new commandment that I write to you, but an old commandment which you had from the beginning. The old commandment is the word which you heard.
verses.2:8: Yet again, I write to you a new commandment, which is true in Him and in you, for the darkness is passing away and the true light already shines.
verses.2:9: He who says he is in the light, yet hates his brother, is in the darkness even until now.
verses.2:10: He who loves his brother abides in the light, and in him there is no occasion for stumbling.
verses.2:11: But he who hates his brother is in the darkness and walks in the darkness, and he does not know where he goes, for the darkness has blinded his eyes.
verses.2:12: I write to you, little children, because your sins have been forgiven you for the sake of His name.
verses.2:13: I write to you, fathers, because you have come to know Him who is from the beginning. I write to you, young men, because you have overcome the wicked one.
verses.2:14: I have written to you, children, because you have come to know the Father. I have written to you, fathers, because you have come to know Him who is from the beginning. I have written to you, young men, because you are strong, and the word of God abides in you, and you have overcome the wicked one.
verses.2:15: Do not love the world, nor the things in the world. If anyone loves the world, the Father's love is not in him;
verses.2:16: for everything in the world—the lust of the flesh, and the lust of the eyes, and the arrogance of life—is not from the Father, but is from the world.
verses.2:17: And the world is passing away, along with its lust; yet he who does the will of God abides forever.
verses.2:18: Children, it is the last hour; and just as you heard that antichrist is coming, even now many antichrists have arisen, by which we know that it is the last hour.
verses.2:19: They went out from us, yet they were not of us; for if they had been of us, they would have remained with us; rather, they departed that they might be made manifest, that none of them are of us.
verses.2:20: And you have an anointing from the Holy One, and you all know.
verses.2:21: I did not write to you because you do not know the truth, but because you know it, and because no lie comes from the truth.
verses.2:22: Who is the liar, except he who denies that Jesus is the Christ? This one is the antichrist, he who denies the Father and the Son.
verses.2:23: Everyone who denies the Son does not have the Father either; he who confesses the Son has the Father as well.
verses.2:24: As for you, let that which you heard from the beginning abide in you. If what you heard from the beginning abides in you, you also shall abide in the Son and in the Father.
verses.2:25: And this is the promise which He Himself promised to us: eternal life.
verses.2:26: These things I have written to you concerning those who seek to lead you astray.
verses.2:27: And as for you, the anointing which you received from Him abides in you, and you have no need that anyone should teach you; rather, as His anointing teaches you concerning all things—and it is true, and is no lie—just as it has taught you, abide in Him.
verses.2:28: And now, little children, abide in Him, so that when He is manifested we may have boldness and not shrink in shame from Him at His coming.
verses.2:29: If you know that He is righteous, you know that everyone who does righteousness has also been born of Him.
verses.3:1: Behold what manner of love the Father has given to us, that we should be called children of God—and so we are! For this reason the world does not know us, because it did not know Him.
verses.3:2: Beloved, now we are children of God, and it has not yet been manifested what we shall be. We know that when He is manifested, we shall be like Him, for we shall see Him just as He is.
verses.3:3: And everyone who has this hope set on Him purifies himself, even as He is pure.
verses.3:4: Everyone who commits sin also commits lawlessness; and sin is lawlessness.
verses.3:5: And you know that He was manifested that He might take away sins, and in Him there is no sin.
verses.3:6: Everyone who abides in Him does not sin; everyone who sins has neither seen Him nor come to know Him.
verses.3:7: Little children, let no one lead you astray. He who does righteousness is righteous, even as He is righteous.
verses.3:8: He who commits sin is of the devil, for from the beginning the devil has been sinning. To this end the Son of God was manifested, that He might destroy the works of the devil.
verses.3:9: Everyone who has been born of God does not commit sin, for His seed abides in him; and he is not able to sin, because he has been born of God.
verses.3:10: By this the children of God and the children of the devil are made manifest: everyone who does not do righteousness is not of God, nor is he who does not love his brother.
verses.3:11: For this is the message which you heard from the beginning: that we are to love one another,
verses.3:12: not as Cain, who was of the wicked one and slew his brother. And for what reason did he slay him? Because his own works were evil, while those of his brother were righteous.
verses.3:13: Do not marvel, brethren, if the world hates you.
verses.3:14: We know that we have passed out of death into life, because we love the brethren. He who does not love abides in death.
verses.3:15: Everyone who hates his brother is a murderer, and you know that no murderer has eternal life abiding within him.
verses.3:16: By this we have come to know love: that He laid down His life on our behalf. And we ourselves ought to lay down our lives for the brethren.
verses.3:17: But whoever possesses the world's goods, and beholds his brother in need, yet closes his heart against him, how does the love of God abide in him?
verses.3:18: Little children, let us not love in word nor with the tongue, but in deed and in truth.
verses.3:19: By this we shall know that we are of the truth, and we shall reassure our hearts before Him
verses.3:20: in whatever our heart may condemn us, for God is greater than our heart and knows all things.
verses.3:21: Beloved, if our heart does not condemn us, we have boldness toward God,
verses.3:22: and whatever we ask we receive from Him, for we keep His commandments and do those things which are pleasing before Him.
verses.3:23: And this is His commandment: that we should believe in the name of His Son Jesus Christ and love one another, just as He gave commandment to us.
verses.3:24: And he who keeps His commandments abides in Him, and He in him. And by this we know that He abides in us: by the Spirit whom He has given to us.
verses.4:1: Beloved, do not believe every spirit, but examine the spirits, whether they are from God, for many false prophets have gone forth into the world.
verses.4:2: In this way you recognize the Spirit of God: every spirit that confesses Jesus Christ as having come in the flesh is from God,
verses.4:3: and every spirit that does not confess Jesus is not from God; and this is the spirit of the antichrist, of which you have heard that it is coming, and even now it is already in the world.
verses.4:4: You are from God, little children, and have conquered them, for greater is He who is in you than he who is in the world.
verses.4:5: They are from the world; for this reason they speak out of the world, and the world hears them.
verses.4:6: We are from God; the one who knows God hears us, while the one who is not from God does not hear us. From this we recognize the Spirit of truth and the spirit of error.
verses.4:7: Beloved, let us love one another, because love is from God, and everyone who loves has been born of God and knows God.
verses.4:8: The one who does not love has not come to know God, because God is love.
verses.4:9: By this the love of God was made manifest among us: that God has sent His only begotten Son into the world, so that we might live through Him.
verses.4:10: In this lies love: not that we have loved God, but that He loved us and sent His Son as the propitiation for our sins.
verses.4:11: Beloved, if God loved us in this way, we ought also to love one another.
verses.4:12: No one has ever beheld God. If we love one another, God abides in us, and His love is brought to perfection in us.
verses.4:13: By this we know that we abide in Him and He in us: because He has given to us from His Spirit.
verses.4:14: And we ourselves have beheld and bear witness that the Father has sent the Son to be the Savior of the world.
verses.4:15: Whoever confesses that Jesus is the Son of God—God abides in him, and he in God.
verses.4:16: And we have known and have put our faith in the love that God has toward us. God is love; and the one who abides in love abides in God, and God abides in him.
verses.4:17: By this means love has been brought to perfection with us, so that we may have confidence in the day of judgment, because just as He is, so also are we in this world.
verses.4:18: There is no fear in love; rather, perfect love drives out fear, because fear carries punishment, and the one who fears has not been brought to perfection in love.
verses.4:19: We love, because He loved us first.
verses.4:20: If someone says, "I love God," yet hates his brother, he is a liar; for the one who does not love his brother whom he has seen is unable to love God whom he has not seen.
verses.4:21: And we have this commandment from Him: that the one who loves God must also love his brother.
verses.5:1: Everyone who believes that Jesus is the Christ has been born of God, and everyone who loves the One who gives birth loves also the one who has been born of Him.
verses.5:2: In this way we know that we love the children of God: whenever we love God and keep His commandments.
verses.5:3: For this is what the love of God is, that we keep His commandments; and His commandments are not burdensome,
verses.5:4: because all that has been born of God conquers the world. And this is the victory that has conquered the world: our faith.
verses.5:5: And who is the one who conquers the world, except the one who believes that Jesus is the Son of God?
verses.5:6: This is the One who came by water and blood—Jesus Christ; not by the water only, but by the water and by the blood. And it is the Spirit who testifies, because the Spirit is the truth.
verses.5:7: For there are three who bear witness:
verses.5:8: the Spirit and the water and the blood, and the three agree as one.
verses.5:9: If we accept the testimony of men, the testimony of God is greater; for this is the testimony of God, that He has borne witness concerning His Son.
verses.5:10: The one who believes in the Son of God has the testimony within himself; the one who does not believe God has made Him a liar, because he has not believed in the testimony that God has borne concerning His Son.
verses.5:11: And the testimony is this: that God gave eternal life to us, and this life is in His Son.
verses.5:12: The one who has the Son has the life; the one who does not have the Son of God does not have the life.
verses.5:13: I have written these things to you, that you may know that you possess eternal life—to you who believe in the name of the Son of God.
verses.5:14: And this is the boldness that we have before Him: that if we ask anything according to His will, He listens to us.
verses.5:15: And if we know that He listens to us in whatever we ask, we know that we possess the requests we have asked from Him.
verses.5:16: If anyone sees his brother committing a sin that does not lead to death, he shall ask, and He will give him life—to those who commit sin not leading to death. There is a sin leading to death; I do not say that he should pray concerning that.
verses.5:17: All unrighteousness is sin, yet there is sin that does not lead to death.
verses.5:18: We know that everyone who has been born of God does not sin; rather, the One who was born of God keeps him, and the evil one does not touch him.
verses.5:19: We know that we are from God, and the entire world lies under the power of the evil one.
verses.5:20: And we know that the Son of God has come and has given us understanding, so that we may know the True One; and we are in the True One, in His Son Jesus Christ. This One is the true God and eternal life.
verses.5:21: Little children, guard yourselves from idols.

notes.1:1: The Greek begins with the neuter relative pronoun ("That which"), emphasizing the totality of the apostolic message incarnate in Christ, and shifts from perfect verbs ("have heard," "have seen") to aorist verbs ("beheld," "touched").
notes.1:4: The critical Greek text reads "our joy" (hemon) rather than "your joy" (hymon), expressing the shared fullness of joy between the apostles and their readers in fellowship with God.
notes.2:1: Greek parakletos ("Advocate") denotes one called alongside to plead on another's behalf; in the Gospel of John the same term designates the Holy Spirit.
notes.2:2: Greek hilasmos ("propitiation") refers to an atoning sacrifice that turns away wrath and removes the guilt of sin.
notes.2:14: Following the critical Greek verse division, "I have written to you, children" begins 2:14 rather than closing 2:13, marking a shift from present-tense "I write" (grapho) to aorist "I have written" (egrapsa) and from teknia ("little children") to paidia ("children").
notes.2:20: The critical Greek text reads pantes ("you all know") rather than panta ("you know all things").
notes.3:1: The critical Greek text includes the emphatic clause kai esmen ("and so we are"), affirming the present reality of believers' adoption as God's children.
notes.3:2: Greek ean phanerothe has no explicit subject and may be rendered either "when He is manifested" (matching 2:28) or "when it is manifested" (referring to what believers shall be).
notes.3:6: The Greek present-tense forms of hamartano ("sin") here and in 3:8-9 are widely understood to describe persistent, habitual sinning rather than a claim to sinless perfection (cf. 1:8-2:1).
notes.3:20: The Greek contains two occurrences of hoti; following standard critical grammar, the first is taken with ean as indefinite ("in whatever") and the second as causal ("for"), linking 3:20 directly to 3:19.
notes.4:3: The earliest Greek manuscripts read simply "does not confess Jesus," whereas later manuscripts expand the clause to echo verse 2 ("Jesus Christ having come in the flesh").
notes.4:9: The Greek adjective monogenes, traditionally rendered "only begotten," emphasizes Christ's status as the unique, one-and-only Son of God.
notes.4:19: The Greek critical text omits an explicit object ("Him") after "We love," presenting love broadly as the believer's response to God's prior love.
notes.5:7: In the earliest Greek manuscripts, verses 7 and 8 name only the three witnesses (the Spirit, the water, and the blood); the Trinitarian expansion ("the Father, the Word, and the Holy Spirit," known as the Comma Johanneum) entered Greek manuscripts only in the late medieval period from Latin tradition.
notes.5:16: The identity of "a sin leading to death" is debated (often understood as hardened apostasy or final rejection of Christ), and the unstated subject of "He will give him life" is ordinarily understood to be God.
notes.5:18: The Greek critical text distinguishes the believer ("everyone who has been born of God," perfect participle) from Christ ("the One who was born of God," aorist participle) who "keeps him" (auton), rather than the later variant "keeps himself" (heauton).
notes.5:20: "This One" (houtos) most naturally refers to its nearest antecedent, "Jesus Christ," affirming His full deity, though some interpreters take it to refer back to "the True One" (God the Father).
